A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same byte-level transformer compression study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original compression experiments, training and context-size sweeps, runtime measurements and supplementary analyses in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds JPEG-XL measurements and an evaluation-dataset-size analysis in Figure 7.

M1.justification: Both use frozen byte-level decoder-only transformers, sequential log-loss training and arithmetic coding. v2 clarifies next-byte predictions, the absence of a separate compression head and teacher-forced evaluation without establishing a changed algorithm or architecture.

E1.justification: The training sources, seven modality mixtures and Reddit, CelebA HQ and LibriSpeech evaluation coverage are retained. Figure 7 varies evaluation-data quantity within this coverage; it does not introduce a new population, domain or task.

E2.justification: v2 adds JPEG-XL alongside the retained JPEG 2000, PNG, FLAC, gzip, LZMA2 and Bellard baselines in Figure 2 and Tables A2–A3. Izacard et al. is newly discussed but explicitly excluded from evaluation.

E3.justification: Figure 7 introduces evaluation across different test-data sizes using models selected for their performance on 1GB. The existing 1GB comparisons, training budgets, preprocessing and hyperparameter sweeps remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds an evaluation-size sensitivity analysis examining when model-storage overhead makes neural compression competitive (Section 5, Figure 7). Existing modality-mixture, scaling, context-size, sliding-window and parameter-compression analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The retained analyses and added results do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing numerical table entries are unchanged. v2 adds JPEG-XL's image ratio of 0.260 and runtime of 871 seconds, making it better in compression ratio than both the transformer (0.285) and Bellard (0.281). Figure 7 also adds compression-ratio curves across evaluation sizes.

T1.justification: The Shannon entropy, cross-entropy/KL argument, log-loss objective and adjusted compression-ratio definition are unchanged. Splitting v1's Equation 1 into two numbered equations and changing the ratio's notation do not introduce new mathematical reasoning or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract extends the claimed advantage to JPEG-XL, replacing its earlier JPEG 2000 example. The central small-model, multimodal-training and weak-transfer claims remain unchanged. The JPEG-XL claim conflicts with v2's Table A2, where JPEG-XL performs better.

C2.justification: v2 adds specific limitations concerning untested transfer-learning strategies and alternative architectures, and explains the choice of runtime rather than FLOPS comparisons. Appendix A also newly asserts that the listed study ingredients are necessary for strong performance, without corresponding necessity tests.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents matching training and evaluation context sizes, direct use of next-byte predictions by arithmetic coding, and teacher forcing. It specifies default JPEG-XL settings. Existing appendix hyperparameters, data-processing instructions and hardware disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: New Appendix A and Table A1 substantially expand positioning against Bellard and Delétang through comparisons of model scale, training regime, modalities, parameter accounting and ablation coverage. Additional citations address JPEG-XL, other transformer compressors, in-context learning and alternative byte-processing architectures.

P1.justification: The abstract, much of the main-text prose, captions and conclusion are extensively condensed and rewritten. v2 expands introductory and method explanations, adds Future Work and Impact Statement passages, and inserts a prior-work appendix before the retained experimental appendices.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from one column to a two-column conference layout, with extensive figure resizing and relocation, including placing Figures 5 and 6 alongside one another. v2 also adds Figure 7 and Table A1, and adds JPEG-XL columns and a baseline line to existing displays.

improvement.justification: The JPEG-XL comparison, evaluation-size analysis and method clarifications strengthen the evidence and explanation. However, v2 claims superiority over JPEG-XL despite reporting 0.260 for JPEG-XL versus 0.285 for its transformer. New Appendix A also contradicts the main text by saying its model parameters need not be counted. These useful additions coexist with new scientific inconsistencies, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
